consensus_findings.description: D3 gives every principal, including service-identity-reader, a one-use SecretID and a client token bounded by token_max_ttl (the current seeder sets 24h), and states that after max TTL 'the principal needs a newly issued protected bundle' as an operator action. Combined with D4 (deny all new API-key authentication 120s after the last good snapshot), a long-running coordinator loses every agent login once per token_max_ttl until a human re-runs the seeder. That converts a rotation feature into a scheduled outage. Resolution: for the two service principals require periodic (renewable, `token_period`) tokens or `token_max_ttl=0`, or specify an authorized automated rebootstrap path; add a COORD scenario 'identity-reader token outlives max TTL without operator action' and record the choice in the topology contract (a per-principal `token_policy` field).

Critical: The coordinator plan replaces api_key_identities but does not explicitly replace the separate api_keys allowlist. Current ApiConfig.from_env retains COORDINATION_API_KEYS and derives an allowlist only once, while _principal_for_api_key accepts any key in that list even when no identity row exists. A rotated key could therefore stay authorized after snapshot replacement or an old static key could authenticate as an unbound principal after configured OpenBao failure.

Critical: wp-dispatch may edit only api_key_resolver.py and its tests, but review_dispatcher.py still passes openbao_role_id plus api_key_env to resolve() and constructs those values from agent roster fields. The new canonical-principal/requested-vendor lookup cannot be called from this site within the package write scope; leaving it unchanged preserves the legacy role override and environment fallback interface.

Critical: The change removes BAO_SECRET_ID and shared-path agent access, but profile_loader.py still authenticates with OpenBaoConfig.create_client() using BAO_SECRET_ID and reads BAO_SECRET_PATH for coordinator profile secrets. No work package can edit profile_loader.py. The plan promises coordinator-internal and dynamic-database secret behavior remains unchanged without defining how this live consumer will authenticate after the configuration change.

Critical: The seeder currently receives one flat .secrets.yaml document, while the plan requires per-agent API-key documents and per-vendor documents. Design D3 acknowledges ambiguous mappings but neither the contracts nor tasks define the explicit operator input format or how a flat source key maps to each destination. Without this, the seeder cannot populate all required paths deterministically or preflight complete migration before mutation.

Critical: review_dispatcher.py creates a fresh ApiKeyResolver for each dispatch invocation, but the planned bootstrap bundle contains a single-use wrapped SecretID and no persisted client token. After the first process unwraps and logs in, a later dispatch process cannot authenticate from the same bundle. The design says rebootstrap is an operator action after token expiry, yet does not provide a protected token cache or a fresh-bundle delivery path for normal repeated dispatches.

Work package wp-coordinator scope omits agent-coordinator/src/profile_loader.py and its tests, but tasks 3.7 and 3.8 and design D5 explicitly assign renaming internal Bao credential inputs in profile_loader.py to wp-coordinator. In an isolated worktree, edits to profile_loader.py will fail scope boundary checks.

Work package wp-dispatch scope permits writing only api_key_resolver.py and its tests, but task 4.2 explicitly requires updating review_dispatcher.py call sites (lines 3027 and 3068). Because review_dispatcher.py is omitted from write_allow, updating the dispatch call sites to pass canonical principal and vendor cannot be completed within package scope.

Schema openbao-event.schema.json defines additionalProperties: false and lacks an action property, but specs/configuration/spec.md (line 70) mandates: "Every mutation, including retired role, policy, and path removal, SHALL emit an audit record with principal, resource, action, and outcome". Emitting an action property will fail schema validation. Additionally, the resource property regex ^(role|policy|agent_path|vendor_path|identity_snapshot)$ rejects "bootstrap", causing openbao.bootstrap.issued events with resource: bootstrap to fail validation.

In principal-topology.schema.json, agent_kv_path requires pattern ^secret/agents/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, and contracts/README.md line 8 calls secret/agents/<name> the "KV logical path". However, in specs/configuration/spec.md (Scenario CFG-03 and line 21), the logical KV-v2 path is defined as agents/<name> relative to mount secret. Passing secret/agents/<name> to HVAC kv.v2 methods with mount_point="secret" causes HVAC to request /v1/secret/data/secret/agents/<name>, duplicating the mount prefix and violating the OpenBao KV-v2 policy paths.

wp-dispatch's consumer is a short-lived CLI process: review_dispatcher.py instantiates a fresh ApiKeyResolver per run (skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py:2946). With secret_id_num_uses=1 the first run consumes the SecretID and the second run has no bootstrap material and must fail closed per CFG-07. Neither the spec, design, nor bootstrap-bundle contract says where the issued client token is persisted between processes (token sink path, mode, owner, renewal responsibility) or how a process detects it must reuse a token instead of the bundle. Resolution: add to the OpenBao Configuration Dataclass requirement an explicit token-sink contract (0600 file under the 0700 bundle directory, or a documented `BAO_TOKEN` handoff) and a scenario 'second process after bootstrap reuses the renewable token'; add the sink path to bootstrap-bundle.schema.json or a sibling schema.

The BREAKING list removes shared BAO_SECRET_ID and retires secret/coordinator at cutover, while stating coordinator-internal secrets remain unchanged. But secret/coordinator today holds coordinator-internal secrets (DB_PASSWORD, LANGFUSE_*) and is read by agent-coordinator/src/profile_loader.py:_load_secrets_openbao via BAO_ROLE_ID/BAO_SECRET_ID and by skills/bao-vault/scripts/langfuse_env.sh. Deleting the path or removing BAO_SECRET_ID breaks profile interpolation and coordinator boot in OpenBao mode. The MODIFIED 'OpenBao Secret Backend' requirement also replaces the body that specifies `_load_secrets()` behavior, so archival silently drops those scenarios. Resolution: either project a third service principal (coordinator-internal) with its own path and add it to the topology contract, or scope cutover deletion to the agent/vendor keys within secret/coordinator and keep the existing profile_loader contract text as unchanged scenarios; add profile_loader.py to a package's write_allow if it is touched.

wp-dispatch changes ApiKeyResolver.resolve from (openbao_role_id, api_key_env) to (principal, vendor), and wp-projection makes the registry schema reject `openbao_role_id`. Callers outside every write_allow break: review_dispatcher.py builds SdkVendorAdapter(openbao_role_id=...) at :2585, stores openai_role_ids at :2620, and calls resolve(...) at :3027 and :3068; test_review_dispatcher.py:1358 passes openbao_role_id; agent-coordinator/tests/model_routing/test_agent_endpoints.py:71 and agents_config.py's dict export at :1891 emit the field. Resolution: add skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py and its test to wp-dispatch write_allow, add tests/model_routing/test_agent_endpoints.py to wp-projection, or keep the old resolve signature as a thin adapter for one release.

wp-projection introduces packages/openbao-credentials imported from agent-coordinator/src. The Dockerfile↔src contract (agent-coordinator/CLAUDE.md, enforced by check-docker-imports and docker-smoke-import CI jobs) requires a matching `COPY packages/openbao-credentials/ /packages/openbao-credentials/` in agent-coordinator/Dockerfile and an entry in the smoke-test modules list in .github/workflows/ci.yml:566. Dockerfile is in no package's write_allow, so wp-projection cannot land green in CI and the production image would fail at import. Resolution: add agent-coordinator/Dockerfile to wp-projection write_allow and a task 1.5 'Bundle shared package into runtime image' with the smoke-module update.

Critical: AI-01/AI-02 require rejecting unknown `vendor_credentials` and AI-01's example uses `[openai]`, but the plan never defines the canonical vendor identifier allowlist or its relationship to existing `policy_vendor`/`catalog_vendor` values (`claude`, `codex`, `grok`, …) and env key names (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). Implementers cannot write a deterministic schema/projection rejection or choose `secret/vendors/<vendor>` path names without inventing that vocabulary.

Critical: CFG-03 requires hvac logical KV-v2 paths `agents/<name>` and `vendors/<vendor>` at mount `secret`, but `principal-topology.schema.json` `agent_kv_path` and contracts/README require `secret/agents/<name>`. Passing the schema form into `client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(path=..., mount_point="secret")` yields `secret/data/secret/agents/...`, breaking every adapter read and policy alignment test.

Critical: `wp-dispatch` write_allow covers only `api_key_resolver.py` (+ its test), but live callers in `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py` still construct SDK adapters with `openbao_role_id` and call `ApiKeyResolver.resolve(openbao_role_id, api_key_env)`. After `wp-projection` removes `openbao_role_id` from `agents.yaml`/schema and dispatch switches to principal+vendor lookup, those call sites remain out of scope and keep the old fail-open contract.

Critical: Proposal BREAKING removes shared `BAO_SECRET_ID`, and CFG says it no longer selects a shared agent credential, but current `profile_loader._load_secrets_openbao()` and `skills/bao-vault/scripts/langfuse_env.sh` still authenticate with `BAO_ROLE_ID`+`BAO_SECRET_ID` and read `BAO_SECRET_PATH` defaulting to `coordinator` for non-agent secrets. Neither file appears in any package write_allow, while `OpenBaoConfig.create_client()` (owned by `wp-coordinator`) is their shared auth entrypoint—so implementing the BREAKING change as written either strands coordinator-internal secret loading or forces out-of-scope edits.

Critical: COORD-03 requires readiness to become degraded on a failed refresh while the last-known-good snapshot remains authoritative for authentication for up to 120s, and the OpenAPI delta returns HTTP 503 whenever a required component is degraded. That couples soft degradation to hard probe failure: transient OpenBao blips within the grace window will 503 `/ready` (breaking `skills/validate-feature` smoke expectations and likely orchestrator traffic shedding) even though API-key auth is still supposed to succeed.

Nit: OpenBaoConfig and the current seeder support BAO_MOUNT_PATH, including non-default mounts, but principal-topology.schema.json fixes mount to 'secret' and every policy path in contracts/README.md starts with secret/data. The configuration spec calls secret the default, leaving it unclear whether non-default mounts remain supported or must be rejected during preflight.

Scenario COORD-07 requires the audit event to identify "authorization" as the failure class, but openbao-event.schema.json names the field error_code and restricts it to uppercase enum values like AUTHORIZATION_DENIED; setting failure_class: authorization violates additionalProperties: false, while error_code: authorization violates the enum. Furthermore, scenario COORD-05 and design D4 specify emitting a recovery event on valid refresh, but openbao-event.schema.json lacks a recovery event in its event enum (only openbao.identity.refresh_succeeded exists).

work-packages.yaml contracts.files list omits newly added contract schemas session-cache.schema.json and migration-map.schema.json, and wp-contracts locks.keys does not lock them. These contracts are now required dependencies of tasks 1.3, 2.1, 4.1, and 5.2, but are not tracked as formal contract artifacts in the work package manifest.

The plan specifies that agent credentials reside at secret/data/agents/<name> and vendor credentials at secret/data/vendors/<vendor>, but neither contracts, design, nor specs define the expected JSON document schema/keys inside these KV-v2 documents (e.g. {"api_key": "..."} vs {"key": "..."} vs placeholder name). Producer (bao_seed.py) and consumers (identity-reader snapshot loader, api_key_resolver.py) risk drifting on document key names.

Requirement "Registry Projection Invariant" (specs/agent-identity/spec.md line 60 and scenario AI-09) mandates CI verification of the credential projection alongside existing profile and identity projections in test_registry_projection.py. However, work-packages.yaml does not include agent-coordinator/tests/test_registry_projection.py in wp-projection write_allow scope (only test_agents_config.py is included).

Task 5.1 and Scenario CFG-15 require pinning the live OpenBao container fixture and failing on mutable tags like latest. The repo defines the OpenBao fixture image at agent-coordinator/docker-compose.yml (currently quay.io/openbao/openbao:latest), but docker-compose.yml is not included in wp-integration write_allow scope.

Identity generation today lives in agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py (get_api_key_identities and _resolve_api_key_from_openbao at :945-1060) and is cached once into the global Config singleton by ApiConfig.from_env (config.py:426-451), which _principal_for_api_key reads on every request. agents_config.py is owned by wp-projection, but AI-03..05 and COORD-01..06 are assigned to wp-coordinator, which cannot write that file, and the two packages run in parallel. Nobody is assigned to remove the shared-SecretID path from agents_config.py or to break the config-singleton caching. Resolution: state in wp-projection's description that it strips OpenBao resolution from agents_config.py (static-only), and in wp-coordinator that openbao_identity.py supplies the snapshot to config/coordination_api; add tests/test_agents_config.py assertions accordingly.

The OpenBao Configuration Dataclass requirement says configuration requires BAO_ADDR, a principal-specific RoleID, and a bundle or token, but names no environment variable or path for the bundle directory, the bundle file, the principal selection for the coordinator (identity-reader) versus a dispatching agent, or the token sink. The existing test_openbao_config.py asserts BAO_ROLE_ID/BAO_SECRET_ID semantics that this change deletes. Without an enumerated surface, wp-coordinator and wp-dispatch will invent different variable names. Resolution: enumerate the variables (for example BAO_BOOTSTRAP_DIR, BAO_PRINCIPAL_ID, BAO_TOKEN_FILE) and their precedence in the requirement, and reference them from contracts/README.md.

D4 returns 503 from GET /ready during the 120s last-known-good grace period while authentication still succeeds. Container platforms that key rollout or restart on /ready (the Dockerfile comment at :138 targets Railway's healthcheck) will pull or restart the instance the moment a refresh fails, which discards the grace window the design pays for. Resolution: decide explicitly. Either return 200 with identity: degraded during grace and 503 only after expiry, or document that platform probes must use /live and /ready is operator-facing; encode the choice in contracts/openapi/v1.yaml and a COORD scenario.

wp-integration's tier-A gate runs agent-coordinator/tests/integration/test_openbao_principals.py, but that directory's conftest.py auto-skips when the PostgREST fixture is unreachable and the `integration` marker is defined as requiring Supabase; the CI test-integration job runs only tests/integration/postgres/. A fully skipped live matrix exits 0 and satisfies live_matrix_passed. Resolution: place live Bao tests under a dedicated directory with a conftest that fails (not skips) when the pinned OpenBao service is absent in CI, add the CI service definition, and have the verification step assert a non-zero collected/passed count.

Nit: CFG OpenBao Secret Backend and COORD credential-failure requirements list timeout as a distinct classified failure alongside backend-unavailable, but `openbao-event.schema.json` `error_code` has no timeout member (only `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`). Adapters and audit assertions cannot satisfy the specs without overloading another code or inventing a non-contractual value.

Nit: Service principal AI-11/AI-12 and contracts/README say the egress gateway reads each configured vendor data path, but nothing states how that configured set is derived (union of all agents' `vendor_credentials`, a separate topology field, or operator config). Without that rule, gateway policy projection and the live denial matrix are underspecified.

Nit: OpenAPI readiness `identity` enum includes `disabled`, but COORD requirements/scenarios only discuss `ready`/`degraded`. Current non-OpenBao deployments must keep `/ready` healthy; without a defined `disabled` meaning (BAO_ADDR absent) implementers may mark identity degraded/503 whenever OpenBao is off.

Nit: Existing AppRoles are named from `openbao_role_id` values that differ from registry keys (e.g. `claude-local` → role `claude-code-local`), while the new contract mandates `agent-<name>` (`agent-claude-local`). CFG-10/CFG-13 cover retiring removed agents and deleting `secret/coordinator`, but the first cutover retirement of legacy role/policy names from the `openbao_role_id` era is not specified, so dry-run/apply can leave orphaned roles or fail ownership checks.

The topology schema pins `mount` to const "secret" while the configuration delta says the KV-v2 mount is `secret` by default and the current code honours BAO_MOUNT_PATH. A non-default mount produces a schema-invalid projection. Resolution: change to a slug-typed string with default "secret", or remove BAO_MOUNT_PATH configurability from the spec.

D2 says callers log class, principal ID, path category and correlation ID, but the event schema has additionalProperties false and no correlation_id, and a vendor lookup failure cannot name the vendor because raw paths are forbidden and there is no `vendor` slug field. Operators cannot correlate a dispatch failure to a review run or tell which vendor path was denied. Resolution: add optional `correlation_id` (string) and `vendor` (slug) properties.

CFG-15 forbids a mutable OpenBao image tag for the test fixture, and agent-coordinator/docker-compose.yml:26 currently uses quay.io/openbao/openbao:latest under the openbao profile. That file is in no package's write_allow. Resolution: add agent-coordinator/docker-compose.yml to wp-integration write_allow, or state that the CI fixture is a separate service definition and the compose profile is out of scope.

Section 3's checkpoint sits before tasks 3.5 and 3.6, so readiness wiring lands unchecked; and section 1 is labelled wp-projection while wp-contracts has no task line, so the contracts gate has no tasks.md anchor for the coordinator status renderer. Resolution: move the checkpoint after 3.6 and add a 0.x task for wp-contracts.

AI-05 forbids COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES from supplying identity when OpenBao is configured. agent-coordinator/CLAUDE.md and the existing spec document that override as the operator rollback lever. The proposal's release-level rollback replaces it, which is coherent, but docs/openbao-secret-management.md and CLAUDE.md must be updated in wp-integration so operators do not rely on a lever that no longer exists in OpenBao mode.

Optional: `wp-projection` mutates `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py` and lists `test_agents_config.py` in write_allow, but its verification step only runs `packages/openbao-credentials` tests—so registry schema/`vendor_credentials`/`openbao_role_id` rejection regressions in the coordinator package can merge green.

Approach 1's shared typed adapter boundary with frozen schemas before consumers, plus a DAG that freezes contracts then fans out seeding/coordinator/dispatch over disjoint write scopes, matches the actual three-client drift problem in `bao_seed.py`, `agents_config.py`, and `api_key_resolver.py` without coupling their runtimes.

Bounded identity degradation (30s refresh, ≤120s last-known-good via monotonic age, then deny-new-auth with sanitized audit) is specified with testable COORD scenarios and clock-controlled unit seams, which is the right control for hot reload without dual-read migration.
